signal: Laurel raised a $100M Series C and became a Workday Innovation Partner to scale its AI time platform for professional services.

email.body1:
Vivian, saw Laurel closed a $100M Series C and became a Workday Innovation Partner.

Scaling that fast usually means more in-market firms in play than the team can cover before reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Laurel off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Vivian, quick follow-up for Laurel.

Post-raise, board expectations on pipeline usually jump faster than headcount can. As the head of business development and enablement you feel both sides: more accounts in play and new reps still ramping. The gap shows up late if no one is doing the math.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Laurel needs to hit target this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Vivian, last bit of proof for Laurel.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Laurel's reply rate likely compares to other Series-C startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Vivian, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. The stretch right after a raise is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I will tailor it to Laurel either way.
